text:
one thing i loved about his product is the focus music

most music i've come across is usually a 4–5 minute lo-fi track without lyrics. it's earthy, cinematic, galactic, or whatever

but what i loved about the music here is the unique the scales and melodies (lot of lydian - euphoric feeling and a mix of dorian scales - slightly mysterious feeling)

and more so that no piece of music lasts more than 2–3 minutes. you get that familiar focus music for a while, but then it switches to rain sounds or white noise for a few minutes and then a different piece comes in

this shuffle has been implemented really smartly. instead of having the same kind of music playing continuously, the changes in sound seem to keep my neurodivergent brain more tuned in compared to the average focus music youtube video

text:
Anyone who has played competitive videogames (or done endurance sports!*) knows that there is nothing quite like a visible, trackable ascension up the competency hierarchy (--> see how addictive LoL/CS/any game with a good ranked mode is). 

The few who have made it to the top in those domains, will know that the feeling is only amplified when the ascension promises acceptance into an elite team/guild/collective of equally-good individuals. 

The obvious and biggest difference between videogames/endurance sports and knowledge work is that, while the former have clear KPIs (ELO, Pace/HR) that prove competency, work doesn't. Promethee seems to want to use hours worked/effort/XP as that KPI - I'm not convinced that'll work. 

But the idea is fundamentally correct and has a lot of potential!

text:
I really like the idea of an app quietly tracking what I’m working on throughout the day.

I haven’t even dug into the analytics yet. Eventually I can just hook Claude into the data and ask questions that are actually useful to me.

But the part I already love is the accountability.

If I set myself a goal, I almost always end up working another 10–15 minutes just to hit it. It’s a tiny psychological push, but surprisingly effective.

It starting to feel a bit like Strava for builders.

Social contracts are incredibly powerful. If other people can see that you said you’d build for 4 hours today, you suddenly really want to do those 4 hours.

I also created a guild called Berlin Builders for people building from Berlin.

If anyone else wants to join, come find us or reply/DM me and I’ll add you :)
